item.title: MPs want to scrap far-right TV show over “Hitler was right” item
item.description:
MPs want to scrap far-right TV show over “Hitler was right” item

August 26, 2026

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

Add as a favourite source on Google Add DutchNews as a favourite source on Google

TV broadcaster Ongehoord Nederland (ON!) is facing fresh calls to have its licence revoked in the wake of an online panel show that presented Nazi leader Adolf Hitler as an anti-globalist crusader.

The segment, Let’s Twist Again, featured a clip of Hitler delivering a tirade against a “rootless international clique”, prompting one person in the crowd to shout out: “Jews!”

Presenter Arlette Adriani then asked the two panellists, Joost Niemöller and Raisa Blommestijn, to comment on the statement: “The cosmopolitan elite is compelled to take an essentially hostile position towards the ordinary indigenous people”. Both said they agreed.

MPs from the coalition parties CDA and D66, as well as the left-wing opposition party Pro, tabled questions in parliament asking culture minister Rianne Letschert if ON! should be taken off the air.

The public broadcasting ombudsman Margo Smit said she had received around 20 complaints about the item since it was put online on July 31, most of them in the last week.

“This fragment is proof that this broadcaster is deliberately flouting basic standards,” Pro MP Mohammed Mohandis told RTL.

“Nazi propaganda”

Oufa Oualhadj, for D66, said: “This thinking is bound up with Nazi propaganda and the depiction of people such as Jews as the enemy by presenting them as a rootless international force that supposedly undermines national communities.”

ON!’s director-general Peter Vlemmix said Niemöller and Blommestijn had made it clear during the broadcast that they felt “nothing but disgust for Hitler’s regime and the barbaric consequences of it”.

But he admitted that the channel had “not paid enough attention to the sensitivities around this subject”. “We should have approached them more carefully in this video.”

ON! has faced repeated calls to have its licence withdrawn since it started broadcasting in 2022. It has been fined for broadcasting misleading information and was found to have used discriminatory language when it advertised the post of editor-in-chief with the words: “man or woman, no X”.

Blommestijn received a criminal conviction for discrimination for a social media post in which she used the term “negroid primates” to describe a group of black men who were filmed assaulting a white man.

“Complex” position

Last month a majority of MPs from all three coalition parties and Pro called on Letschert not to renew the broadcaster’s licence next year.

Erik van der Maas, of right-wing liberal party VVD, said: “There is no place in the public network for a broadcaster that is funded by taxpayers’ money but systematically breaks the rules and is not prepared to keep to them.”

But the minister said the legal position was “complex” because the public broadcasting service NPO had not asked her to withdraw ON!’s licence. “That does not take away the concerns about Omroep Nederland,” she said.

The channel’s future is due to form part of a debate in parliament on September 24.

item.title: Hundreds evacuated in Apeldoorn after suspected drugs lab found
item.description:
Hundreds evacuated in Apeldoorn after suspected drugs lab found

August 26, 2026

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

Add as a favourite source on Google Add DutchNews as a favourite source on Google

Around 220 people were evacuated from three apartment blocks in Apeldoorn on Wednesday morning after police found a suspected drugs lab in one of the buildings overnight.

Residents of about 100 homes on the Eburonenstraat were ordered out at around 10am. Officers were alerted after someone reportedly threw fireworks from a balcony, and went on to find weapons and what they believe was a drugs lab inside one of the flats.

One resident has been arrested and is being questioned.

Specialist units are on the scene, including the national dismantling service (LFO), which is called in when chemicals pose a risk to the surrounding area, and a police explosives-safety officer.

Police said they could not yet tell whether there was any danger of an explosion, and the area around the building has been sealed off. A few officers reported feeling unwell from chemical fumes and were checked by ambulance crews, but none needed hospital treatment.

Residents of the two outer blocks were allowed home in the early afternoon. Those in the middle block, where the find was made, are still waiting to return.

The evacuation comes as Dutch police warn that drug producers are increasingly setting up labs in residential areas, bringing the dangers of volatile chemicals into densely populated buildings.

item.title: Dutch tourist believed missing after flooding in Nepal kills 31
item.description:
Dutch tourist believed missing after flooding in Nepal kills 31

August 26, 2026

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

Add as a favourite source on Google Add DutchNews as a favourite source on Google

A Dutch national has been reported missing after severe flooding left on the border between Nepal and Tibet at least 31 people dead and nearly 400 unaccounted for.

The Nepalese tourism authority said a total of 384 visitors were missing in the region, including 291 foreigners. More than 90 people were injured when flash floods engulfed whole villages along the Bhote Khoshi, Trishuli and Narayani rivers.

The Dutch tourist was one of two non-Nepalis, along with an Australian, in a party of 17 travelling with a Kathmandu-based tour operator. Around one-quarter of those unaccounted for are from India.

Nepal’s foreign minister said the floods were triggered by a combination of an earthquake in Tibet and high water in the Bhote Khoshi river, which had been swelled by melting snow.

Bhotekoshi Flash Flood
SITUATION UPDATE -2
Date: August 26, 2026

Preliminary Details of Missing Tourists pic.twitter.com/gxWJfVfKuX

— Nepal Tourism Board (@nepaltourismb) August 26, 2026

The earthquake, measuring 4.4 on the Richter scale, caused an avalanche and a heavy mudslide that poured into the river.

Surveillance footage from the Gyirong County border crossing showed buildings around the checkpoint being submerged by mud and water. Around 4,000 people live in the region, which is a trading hub and a popular base for hikers.

Chinese president Xi Jinping has ordered search and rescue workers to conduct “all-out” efforts to find the missing visitors after state media outlet CCTV reported “major casualties” in the region.

The Dutch foreign affairs ministry said it was monitoring the situation closely. “We are ready to offer consular help if it is necessary,” a spokesman said.

Dutch citizens in the area have been urged to contact their friends and family or call the government’s emergency number on +31 247 247 247.

item.title: Utrecht death shows West Nile virus is circulating in NL
item.description:
Utrecht death shows West Nile virus is circulating in NL

August 26, 2026

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

Add as a favourite source on Google Add DutchNews as a favourite source on Google

A person in Utrecht province has died in hospital after catching West Nile virus in the Netherlands, the public health institute RIVM has said.

The fact it was caught in the Netherlands means the virus is now circulating in the local mosquito population. It is one of three such infections RIVM has recorded so far in 2026, the others infected are still in hospital.

RIVM said it would not release details about the person who died out of respect for the family. A spokesperson described them as elderly and in poor health. The death is not connected to last week’s case in a Utrecht blood donor, the first human infection caught in the Netherlands since 2020.

This year the virus has been detected in Utrecht, Noord-Brabant and Zuid-Holland – in horses, mosquitoes and birds – and RIVM has asked doctors across the country to watch for patients with symptoms of West Nile fever.

Not the start of a pandemic
A single death, even a local one, does not signal a pandemic in the making, because West Nile virus is not the type to cause one. It does not pass from person to person.

People and horses can fall seriously ill, but they are dead ends for the virus: they do not carry enough of it in their blood to reinfect a biting mosquito, so the chain stops with them.

The death does however mark the establishment of the virus in northern Europe, which scientists are linking to warmer weather. It first reached people in the Netherlands in 2020, in a small cluster around Utrecht and Arnhem.

Who is at risk
Most infections go unnoticed, and around 80% of people who catch the virus have no symptoms at all and roughly 19% develop flu-like illness. About 1% go on to serious neurological problems such as inflammation of the brain, and a small number of those die.

Mosquitoes carrying the virus are most active at dusk. In the affected provinces, covering up in the evening lowers the chance of being bitten – though RIVM stresses the odds of catching the virus in the Netherlands, let alone falling ill from it, remain very low.

Separately, the regional public health service GGD Drenthe reported last week that a woman had probably died of West Nile fever after catching it on holiday in south-eastern Europe. That was an imported case, unlike the Utrecht death.

item.title: Cabinet and mayors agree to prosecute motorway protesters
item.description:
Cabinet and mayors agree to prosecute motorway protesters

August 26, 2026

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

Add as a favourite source on Google Add DutchNews as a favourite source on Google

Anyone who blocks a motorway or railway line will in principle face criminal prosecution, the country’s regional mayors, prosecutors and police chief have agreed with justice minister David van Weel.

The joint statement, issued on Tuesday, says the rules apply to everyone “from farmers to climate activists”, though local authorities can still make exceptions case by case.

“Demonstrating is a fundamental right and we protect it,” it reads. “But expressing your opinion is something other than making the motorway or the railway unsafe.”

The move follows a fatal crash during recent farmers’ protests. Two people died and six were injured when a car ran into the back of a tractor-related tailback on the A59 earlier this month.

Nijmegen mayor Hubert Bruls, who chairs the regional mayors and had asked for national rules, said nothing had changed legally – tractors were already banned from motorways – but the confusion had now been removed.

Climate group Extinction Rebellion said it had no intention of stopping. “As long as the government and big business fail to do what is needed, we will continue with peaceful civil disobedience,” the group said, adding that it is already facing prosecution, with a court case due on August 26.

XR, which has blocked the A12 in The Hague dozens of times, said the measure was a distraction. Its activists have been treated far more harshly than farmers over the summer: around 270 were arrested on the A12 last month, while some 80 farmers escaped fines on the A35 because their number plates were taped over.

item.title: Worst drought in 700 years turns wetland into graveyard for fish
item.description:
Worst drought in 700 years turns wetland into graveyard for fish

August 26, 2026

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

Add as a favourite source on Google Add DutchNews as a favourite source on Google

The summer drought has dried up the Zeezuiper, a wetland reserve in Noord-Brabant, for the first time in 700 years, leaving behind hundreds of dead fish.

Forest ranger Erik de Jonge was shocked when he returned from holiday to find the area, usually teeming with geese and wetland birds, had become a barren scrubland, with just a few scattered puddles remaining.

“We’ve seen a lot of droughts here in the last 10 years, but this beats everything,” De Jonge told Omroep Brabant. “This hasn’t happened since 1300.”

Stepping over a pile of dead and rotting fish, he explained: “We can see the fish retreated to the deepest water, but they died because even here the water has disappeared. There are deer running around. It’s unprecedented.”

The leaves have started to fall early because woodland trees such as birch, beech and maple are suffering from heat stress, De Jonge explained. “It looks like autumn, with all the fresh leaves, but it’s the old beeches reacting to the drought.”

Between 60% and 80% of the surrounding heathland is dried up, while the usually abundant berries are sparse and shrivelled.

Migrating birds

That will have an impact on migrating birds that pass through in autumn, De Jonge said. “These are vitamins for the birds that are coming in the next few weeks. Usually they can expect a buffet, but the buffet has dried up.”

Wetlands also play an important role in absorbing CO2 from the surrounding area. “A swamp captures more CO2 than a forest, so this will have negative consequences for the climate,” he said.

Water levels in the Zeezuiper have been falling steadily since the 1970s, but the trend has accelerated in recent years. De Jonge is urging authorities such as the water board to take steps to ensure the area retains as much water as possible when the rain finally returns.

“We’ve been calling for this for years, but we can’t ignore it any longer,” he said.

item.title: Netherlands to miss gas target: What it means for households
item.description:
Netherlands to miss gas target: What it means for households

August 26, 2026

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

Add as a favourite source on Google Add DutchNews as a favourite source on Google

The Netherlands will miss its target for filling its gas reserves before this winter, national gas network operator Gasunie has confirmed.

The shortfall, first reported by NU.nl, would not leave homes cold in a normal winter, Gasunie said, but it does make the country more vulnerable to an exceptionally cold spell or a sudden disruption in supply.

Dutch underground storage sites were about 45% full in late August, compared with roughly 94% at the same point in 2023 and 63% a year ago.

The government’s target, set on Gasunie’s advice, was to fill the reserves to about 80% of capacity by November 1. Levels are currently stuck near 45%, and the minimum EU target is 74%.

Is there enough gas?
For an ordinary winter, Gasunie says supply is secure. Gas continues to arrive through pipelines from Norway, through terminals for liquefied natural gas (LNG), and from small Dutch fields.

The concern is what happens when several things go wrong at once: a long cold spell that also drives up demand in neighbouring countries, for example, alongside a fault at a pipeline or an LNG terminal.

“Under normal conditions I am not extremely worried about the amount of gas in storage,” energy expert René Peters of research institute TNO told broadcaster NOS. “The risk lies mainly in situations where several problems occur at the same time.”

Why are reserves low?
The main reason the reserves are low is that commercial energy firms have stored almost no gas. Summer gas prices have been higher than the expected winter price, so storing gas now to sell later does not pay off. Traders have linked the higher gas prices partly to the war around Iran.

To make up the gap, the state has stepped in. State energy company EBN is storing gas on the government’s instruction in Bergermeer, Norg and Grijpskerk, and says it is on schedule to reach its 80 TWh ceiling. Gasunie warned in June that filling was going too slowly.

The cost to households
For most households the effect will be on price rather than supply. Refilling reserves with expensive summer gas feeds through into energy costs, and households on variable or dynamic contracts tend to feel that first, which is worth bearing in mind when choosing an energy contract.

Gasunie has urged the government to create a strategic gas reserve for emergencies. One option being discussed is keeping part of the Groningen gas field – shut down in 2024 after extraction triggered hundreds of earthquakes – available purely as an emergency supply, a politically contentious idea in a region still dealing with the damage.

The cabinet is due to update parliament on the reserves, and on possible further steps, in September.

item.title: Mondriaan painting set to fetch €30m at auction later this year
item.description:
Mondriaan painting set to fetch €30m at auction later this year

August 26, 2026

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

Add as a favourite source on Google Add DutchNews as a favourite source on Google

A painting by the Dutch artist Piet Mondriaan is expected to sell for more than €30 million when it goes under the hammer later this year.

The work, Composition III, dates from 1920, the year Mondriaan returned to Paris to develop his distinctive abstract style of Neo-Plasticism.

The painting, which has been in a private collection for the last 25 years, is expected to fetch the highest price this autumn when London auction house Christie’s puts it up for sale on October 14.

“It is a very rare work from the year that you really see Mondriaan finding his feet and developing his neoplastic theory as an artist,” Keith Gill, head of impressionist and modern art at Christie’s said.

Mondriaan finished just eight paintings in 1920, five of which are owned by major museums such as the Stedelijk Museum in Amsterdam, the Tate in London and the Museum of Modern Art in New York.

Christie’s estimates it will sell for between £20 mln and £20 mln (€23 mln-€35 mln), but Gill said that could prove to be a conservative estimate.

“Given the importance of this masterpiece and the outstanding condition it is in, it could easily fetch more,” he told the Telegraaf.

The record price for a Mondriaan was set in November 1922, when Composition no. II sold for $51 million (€49.4 mln) at Sotheby’s in New York.

item.title: New in NL: Should you go for a traditional Dutch bank or go neo?
item.description:
Partner content

New in NL: Should you go for a traditional Dutch bank or go neo?

August 26, 2026

The financial services industry in the Netherlands has changed enormously in recent years, shaken up by the internet, changing customer demand and banking apps. So what is best for you – an account with a more traditional bank or an online-only version?

One of the first things you need to do when establishing yourself in the Netherlands is to set up a bank account, so you are ready to pay rent, use public transport and access your salary as soon as you hit the ground.

The rise of fintech – technology-driven financial services – and neo banks, which are online-only alternatives to traditional banks, has increased the choices available to expats, but there are some things to consider before you decide what sort of bank to go for.

Ask questions in English

For a start, think about how you want to communicate with your bank. Are you happy using a chatbot to get answers to your questions – or, as often happens, one that fails to give you a proper answer at all? Or would you prefer to speak directly to a human being?

ABN Amro, for example, has a team of English-language advisors who are there to answer your questions by phone or online. You can set up a face-to-face online meeting with one of them from anywhere in the world, before you have even arrived.

Decades of experience

Another important difference between more traditional banks and the fintechs comes down to experience. Traditional banks have many more years of experience in helping clients and know what makes them tick. ABN Amro has been serving hundreds of thousands of internationals and expats for over 25 years, devising products which are directly tailored to their needs.

In addition, the traditional Dutch banks are all rooted in the Netherlands, so they are well versed in their domestic market and understand local financial needs.

Expat banking can be complicated

Unlike neo banks, traditional banks also operate high-street branches where you can go personally to sort out paperwork or other issues which are difficult to deal with online. Expats, in particular, may have more complicated financial needs, such as being paid a salary in a different currency.

In addition, neo banks and fintechs mainly offer current and savings accounts but not the other financial services which you need to establish yourself in the Netherlands, which means you cannot take care of all your financial needs under one roof.

That’s fine, of course, if you are happy shopping around. But if simplicity and ease are important to you, it would be sensible to look at a bank which offers wider services.

Think insurance, for example, or pensions, or a mortgage – if you are planning to stay in the Netherlands for longer. Traditional banks cater to your long-term financial needs, not just your immediate ones, offering more specialist wealth management and private banking services as well as instant payments and cash withdrawals.

Online banking services

Of course, traditional banks have evolved alongside digital-first providers, offering many of the same online banking features that customers expect today. You can bank via your phone, use your (online) direct debit card at home and abroad, seamlessly make and accept payments in other currencies and keep a close eye on your daily spending patterns – all of which are part of the modern approach to banking.

In that sense, the difference between a high-street and an online bank is virtually non-existent. The main differences become apparent when customers need personal support or access to a broader range of financial services which the neo banks don’t offer.

In fact, there may even be financial advantages to opening an account with a more traditional bank! ABN Amro, for example, is currently offering up to €175 cashback for new customers who open their first current account.

item.title: Feyenoord face ban from Nijmegen for setting off fireworks
item.description:
Feyenoord face ban from Nijmegen for setting off fireworks

August 26, 2026

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

Add as a favourite source on Google Add DutchNews as a favourite source on Google

Feyenoord fans have been barred from travelling to the team’s next two away matches in the Eredivisie after fireworks were let off in Cambuur Leeuwarden’s stadium when the teams met at the weekend.

Seven home fans were injured after the fireworks erupted in the away supporters’ enclosure in De Kooi stadium on Sunday. Police and the club are investigating how fans managed to smuggle large quantities into the stadium.

The club said on Wednesday it had decided not to allow supporters into the away end for the away matches at NEC Nijmegen on September 5 and PEC Zwolle on September 13.

“Obviously this is the last thing we want, but we feel we have no alternative after what went on in Leeuwarden,” managing director Robert Eenhoorn said on the club’s website.

“It means coach Giovanni van Bronckhorst’s team will have to play on foreign soil twice without the backing of their own supporters.“

On Tuesday, the mayor of Nijmegen, Hubert Bruls, said he would ban Feyenoord fans from the Goffertstadion unless those responsible for the fireworks at Cambuur were arrested.

Feyenoord won the match in Leeuwarden 5-2 after a 20-minute break. Referee Danny Makkelie later questioned guidelines that say a match should be abandoned if a player is struck by objects thrown from the crowd, but nothing about injuries to supporters.

“It’s an agreement made between the clubs, not us,” Makkelie explained. “I don’t know what the reason for it is, because it’s just as bad whether players or supporters are hit.”
